straattaal.name: Straattaal
straattaal.about: Amsterdam's young street talk: Dutch mixed with words from Sranan, Papiamento, Moroccan Arabic, Berber and English. Mattie, fissa, doekoe.

greet: Hi! Did you cycle in through all that wind?
Hello! Are you at the meetup in Noord tonight?
Hi there, lovely to finally meet in person!
reply: All good, thanks, still learning to dodge tourists in the bike lane.
Great, just found a flat, after four months.
Not bad, the ferry was lovely this morning.
sunny: Sun's out, the whole city will be on the canals.
Gorgeous, let's take lunch outside by the IJ.
Sunny and no wind, a miracle.
rain: Rain and headwind, the classic Amsterdam combo.
Grab your rain trousers, it's coming down.
Wet day, perfect for a brown café.
The Buienradar says it stops in ten minutes. Sure.
bye: Take care, see you at the borrel!
busy: Sorry, got a call in five, catch you later!
Running for the ferry, talk soon!
Late for a demo at the office, see you!
Busy day, let's grab a coffee tomorrow?
Can't stop, my bike's parked badly!

greet: Hoi! Ook op weg naar kantoor?
sunny: Prachtig weer, het Vondelpark ligt vol.
rain: Het regent weer, echt Hollands weer.
Volgens Buienradar is het zo droog.
busy: Ik heb zo een meeting, doei!
Ik mis mijn pont, tot later!

greet: Yo mattie, wat ga je doen?
sunny: Mooi weer, fissa in het park?
Chill weer, we gaan naar buiten.
Zonnetje, ik trek mijn nieuwe patta's aan.
rain: Natte dag, ik blijf in de osso.
Regen, mattie, ik ga niet naar buiten.
Alles nat, ik ga chillen binnen.
busy: Ik moet gaan, spreek je later!
Geen tijd mattie, ik ben laat!

touts: Let op: bij deze halte kunt u niet uitstappen.
Mind the gap between the train and the platform.
hawkers: Verse stroopwafels, warm van de plaat!
Fresh stroopwafels, warm off the iron!
Three kilos of mandarins, two euros!
Battered fish bites, nice and hot!
Doughnut balls, ten for ten euros! (around New Year)
small_talk: The ferry to Noord was packed with bikes again.
My bike got stolen, third one this year.
Took me six months to find a flat, and it's in Diemen.
Tourists keep walking in the bike lane on the Damrak.
The Albert Cuyp has the best stroopwafels, don't argue.
King's Day is coming, everyone's buying orange.
Everyone at the Zuidas switches to English the second you hesitate.
The Noord/Zuidlijn changed my commute completely.
Headwind both ways, how is that even possible?
